title: PowerStep: Memory-Efficient Adaptive Optimization via l_p-Norm Steepest Descent: the convergence theorem with its explicit constants (Theorem 1)
author: Yao Lu, Dengdong Fan, Shixun Zhang, Yonghong Tian
work: PowerStep: Memory-Efficient Adaptive Optimization via l_p-Norm Steepest Descent
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the paper's convergence theorem for its memory-efficient adaptive method, printed as Theorem 1 at source0.tex lines 163-172 and delivered with the paper's own complete proof (the appendix subsection at lines 852-918). The statement is a full non-asymptotic rate for the method under an l_p-norm smoothness assumption and a bounded stochastic oracle: a stationarity bound of the form C_1/sqrt(T) + C_2/T plus a residual proportional to the average noise moment, with explicit dependence on the smoothness and gradient constants and the momentum parameter. The proof is the paper's own assembly over the retained lemmas: it integrates the smoothness assumption along the update segment, bounds the expected objective decrease, sums over the horizon, substitutes the alignment, drift and noise-moment lemmas together with the geometric moment bound for the momentum buffer, and then re-arranges into the master bound and the corrected rate, finishing with the Euclidean-to-native norm conversions. This is a research-level convergence analysis with its own drift decomposition rather than a qualifying-examination computation; the unit is H2.
